originality.rationale: The arXiv 2610.31319v1 fixed-particle theorem proves only first-order independent diffusion and bounds the near-neighbour occupation by O(1/n) in Proposition 6.8; it does not give the rescaled *random predictable centre-bracket deficit* or its joint independent Brownian-centre law. The primary full texts 2512.20412v1 and 2610.13308v1 treat different hydrodynamic or positive-density observables. Fan 1410.3585 explicitly proves joint reflected-walk/local-time convergence, and Denisov--Wachtel 1412.6184 establishes reflected local-time universality, so those ingredients are not new. The distinguishing claim requires a two-particle generator, the exact quadratic-bracket coefficient and its joint FCLT; no compared source states or clearly implies that complete observable-level claim without further model-specific derivation. Priority risk from broader particle-system theorems remains.

value.rationale: Proposition 6.8 of the source proves an O(1/n) contribution of exclusion to the atomic quadratic variation in one dimension, but the typical random fluctuation and its distribution are unresolved by that upper bound. The complete non-Gaussian regulator process, its exact independent coupling to leading Gaussian motion, the atom/one-time tail and exact strictly positive asymptotic variance deficit are a motivated second-order answer for the simplest fixed-particle exclusion model. Not a renaming of local time alone: identifies the physically observable compensator of blocked center jumps and an exact coefficient not a general theorem for arbitrary particles.
